name: acme-partner-access-path-single-vendor
description: ILLUSTRATIVE Approach-1 example (single pipeline, multi-device) for firewall-policy-use-case.md §3 Approach 1 — the SAME partner-HTTPS path, but all three firewalls are ONE vendor (PAN-OS) owned by ONE team. Modeled as a SINGLE network-provisioning pipeline (Harvest → Design → Author → Review), NOT a program: no Program Architect, no interface contract, no DAG of pipelines, no per-team gates. NOT runnable as-is (no live PAN-OS harvest service wired; the pan-os protocol is notional). Design worked-example.
domainProtocol: network-provisioning (notional PAN-OS variant — one pipeline reads and designs all three devices)
harvestDescriptor: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paichart/paichart/main/descriptors/<panos-readonly-descriptor>.json (NOT YET PUBLISHED — illustrative; ONE descriptor, three device targets)

endToEndFlow.notes: One vendor, one team → ONE pipeline. The end-to-end consistency (and any interdependency) is resolved INSIDE the single designer's context: one Design stage holds all three devices at once and produces the coherent rule set. Even a source-NAT — the exact thing that forces Approach 3 ACROSS vendors — is a non-issue here: the same designer picks the pool AND writes the downstream match rules in one design turn, so there is no cross-pipeline chaining to coordinate. Program machinery (contract, DAG, per-team gates) would be pure overhead.
